entities.name: Idomeneus of Lampsacus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Idomeneus of Lampsacus (c. 350 – 280 BCE) was a pivotal Greek philosopher and Epicurean thinker who laid the groundwork for the development of Epicureanism in ancient Greece.

A student of Epicurus in Athens, Idomeneus became a prominent figure in the Epicurean school of thought, emphasizing the importance of reason, self-sufficiency, and the pursuit of happiness. His teachings had a lasting impact on Western philosophy, influencing thinkers such as Lucretius and the Stoics.

Although the exact details of his life are shrouded in mystery, Idomeneus' philosophical contributions had a profound effect on the development of Epicureanism, which in turn shaped the intellectual landscape of the ancient world.

One of the most significant legacies of Idomeneus is his role in shaping the Epicurean concept of 'ataraxia' or 'freedom from mental distress.' This idea would go on to influence the development of Stoicism and other philosophical schools, cementing Idomeneus' place as a key figure in the history of Western philosophy.
